note: Synthetic positive and negative controls mapped to AC-01..AC-09 of the approved planning artifact contract. Controls are inputs for model-driven behavioral evaluation: inspect generated artifacts, approval evidence, and whether an implementer was dispatched. 'files' declares repository state (null means the path must not exist); 'dispatch' records the required implementer-dispatch verdict; 'inspect' lists paths whose content or absence is evidence. Derived from sanitized synthetic scenarios; no private session data is included.

ac-02.title: First vocabulary: a meaningful glossary appears only when terms resolve

positive.input: We settled it: 'cancellation' means the whole order stops before fulfillment, and 'proration' means charging the used fraction. Capture that and hand the design to planning.
positive.expected: Create the root CONTEXT.md lazily now that two real terms are resolved, using the domain glossary format, and record the vocabulary outcome of the capture checkpoint with the execution handoff; no placeholder sections or fictional terms are added.

negative.input: Setup reran on this project; make sure the domain documentation exists before we continue.
negative.expected: No term was resolved in this request, so no glossary is created: 'No new terms is a valid outcome' is reported rather than fabricating a placeholder CONTEXT.md or fictional domain names.

ac-03.title: Multiple contexts: ownership is asked for, never invented as a root glossary

positive.input: In the billing context, 'dunning' means the automated retry ladder for failed charges. Record it.
positive.expected: Follow the real context map and record the resolved term only in src/billing/CONTEXT.md; no root CONTEXT.md is created or touched for a configured multi-context project.

negative.input: Add 'fulfillment hold' to the glossary. It could belong to either the ordering or the shipping context.
negative.expected: Stop and ask which real context owns the term or request a real context map; do not create a root CONTEXT.md just because the map is absent, and do not choose an owner silently.

ac-04.title: Selective decisions: an ADR only for qualifying approved trade-offs

positive.input: Decision approved: the write model is event-sourced on Postgres instead of CRUD tables. It is expensive to reverse, future readers will ask why, and we evaluated the document-store alternative first. Record it.
positive.expected: Create the first ADR under docs/adr/ in the established format recording why the approved trade-off was made, then return to the calling design workflow; the ADR records rationale, not behavior or acceptance criteria.

negative.input: Also, we'll defer browser support until next quarter. Write an ADR for that too so nothing is lost.
negative.expected: Decline the ADR: a temporary scope choice fails the selective criteria (not hard to reverse, not surprising, no real evaluated alternatives). Report explicitly that no ADR is warranted and keep the deferral as ordinary scope history instead of manufacturing a decision record.

negative.expected: Refuse the bounded shortcut: cross-cutting behavior with many interacting rules is architectural work requiring shaping and an approved behavioral specification. Report the missing approved behavioral source instead of dispatching a writer on an unshaped request.
